I call on Ms. Marin for a proclamation. Whereas March has been officially designated as Arts in Our Schools Month, encouraging communities across the nation to focus on dance, music, theater, and visual arts education.

This month serves as a reminder that all students deserve access to and equity in the delivery of dance, music, theater, and visual arts education. And whereas Fairfax County Public Schools has a thriving fine and performing arts education program with over 630 music educators, over 46,000 students in instrumental and chorus programs, over 430 art educators, and over 20,000 students in elective secondary art, FCPS hosts one of the largest theater education programs in the United States with nearly 60 theater teachers and more than 6,500 theater students.

FCPS Dance has programs at the elementary and high school levels, dance, music, theater, and visual arts students at FCPS demonstrate the importance of quality, fine, and performing arts education programs to the lives of young people. And whereas FCPS Arts programs are known throughout the state and country as a model of excellence, emphasizing conceptual learning, personal relevance, and innovation, in March and throughout the spring, FCPS School Pyramids celebrate the arts with pyramid art shows exhibiting the works of elementary, middle, and high school students in each community.

Each year, middle and high school artists are recognized throughout the FCPS Artifacts Awards, the Scholastic Art Awards, and other art recognition programs. And whereas the FCPS Music Program consistently receives recognition as a recipient of the Best Communities for Music Education Award from the National Association of Music Merchants, the 6th Grade All-County Choral Festival is recognized as one of the largest elementary choir events in the nation.

FCPS Secondary Ensembles garner accolades at prestigious events including the Virginia State Music Conference, Midwest Band and Orchestra Clinic, National Band Association, and American Choral Directors Association. Our schools have been honored with several national distinctions such as the Sudler Flag of Honor, the Sudler Cup of Distinction, the VMEA Blue Ribbon Award, and the VMEA Honor Band Award. And whereas FCPS Theater and Dance offer a vast array of curricular and extracurricular art experiences, including dance events and showcases, plays, musicals, drama clubs, improv competitions, student-directed one-act festivals, the VHSL State One-Act Competition, the Brandon-Victor Dixon Awards, and the Cappies.

The Cappies, an international high school program that celebrates theater performance, journalism, and student ownership originated in Fairfax County Public Schools. FCPS theater students and teachers are recognized at this annual gala in Washington, D.C. Now therefore, be it resolved, Fairfax County Public Schools recognizes March as Dance in Our Schools, Music in Our Schools, Theater in Our Schools Month, and Youth Art Month to celebrate and acknowledge every day that fine and performing art education experiences and opportunities are an essential part of every student's well-rounded education.

Agenda Item 3.05, Transgender Day of Visibility Proclamation. I call on Mr. McDaniel for her proclamation. Whereas Fairfax County Public Schools is committed to fostering a safe, welcoming, and inclusive learning environment where every student, employee, and family is respected and empowered.

And whereas Transgender Day of Visibility is observed annually on March 31st to celebrate the lives and contributions of transgender people while raising awareness of the disproportionate discrimination and violence the transgender community continues to face.

And whereas transgender students, families, and staff are integral members of our community whose talents, leadership, and courage enrich our classrooms, strengthen our schools, and inspire all. And whereas, transgender people have made significant contributions throughout history, including early LGBTQIA plus rights movement activists like Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera, artists such as Laverne Cox and Kim Petras, leaders like Sarah McBride, the first openly transgender member of Congress, and Virginia Senator Danica Rome, the first openly transgender state legislature.

Scientists like distinguished neurobiologist Dr. Ben Barres and Dr. Lynn Conway, whose innovations revolutionized computer science and countless others whose courage and achievements have advanced equality and inspired others. And whereas all transgender people have inherent worth and are deserving of respect and dignity from these and other well-known historical and public figures to those for whom it is not safe to live their authentic lives. Wherever they are on their journey, they are valued and valid. And whereas major medical organizations, including the American

Academy of Pediatrics, the American Medical Association, the American Psychological Association, and the American Psychiatric Association have affirmed the validity of transgender identities and support age-appropriate gender-affirming care as evidence-based medically necessary treatment that it significantly improves health outcomes for transgender people.

And whereas transgender youth face significantly higher rates of mental health challenges, largely due to discrimination, rejection, and lack of affirmation, underscoring the critical importance of inclusive schools where transgender students can thrive with research demonstrating that transgender youth who feel supported in their identity show significantly improved academic, social, and emotional outcomes, and whereas transgender students deserve to learn in environments free from discrimination, harassment, bullying, and exclusion, and to have their names, pronouns, and identities honored, and whereas the Fairfax

County School Board stands with and celebrates its transgender students, families, and staff, recognizing the urgency of its charge to foster a responsive, caring, and inclusive culture by reaffirming its commitment to policies that uphold the rights of well-being of transgender individuals, ensuring access to education and employment free from discrimination and grounded in respect, and whereas the Fairfax County School Board recognizes that learning and growth require ongoing reflection,

dialogue, and partnership with students, families, staff, and community members to advance equity and understanding. Now, therefore, be it resolved that the Fairfax County School Board proclaims March 31, 2026 as Transgender Day of Visibility in Fairfax County Public Schools and encourages all to promote a caring culture of equity, inclusivity, and respect for transgender people, not only on this special day, but throughout the entire year as well.
